files.lesson.md: --- order: 17 unit: circles node: AC9M8M03 n2 uses: [AC9M8M03 n1] title: Circle problems summary: "Choose the formula by what you need: C = 2πr for a length round the edge, A = πr² for the space inside. Work backwards from an area with r = √(A ÷ π). Half and quarter circles, rings and tracks are parts of circles added to or taken from other shapes." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A running track, a round garden bed, a pizza deal: is a 30 cm pizza more than twice a 20 cm one? Circle problems need the right formula, sometimes run backwards." connection: pizza-value app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8308 url: http://127.0.0.1:8308/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: circle.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A circle of radius 3 m: A = π × 9 ≈ 28.27 m²." } explainClip: query: { code: "@circle.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "From area back to radius" say: "Which radius gives an area of about twenty-eight?" clip: - caption: { text: "We need an area of about 28.3 m². Try radius 1.", say: "We need about twenty-eight. Try radius one." } - wait: 800 - caption: { text: "Radius 3: π × 9 ≈ 28.27. Found it.", say: "Radius three. Pi times nine. Found it." } - click: Make the radius bigger - click: Make the radius bigger - click: Make the radius bigger - click: Make the radius bigger - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "28.27" } - wait: 1500 --- Ask first: is the answer a **length** round the edge (circumference, $C = 2\pi r$) or the **space** inside (area, $A = \pi r^2$)? ## Predict: a round rug ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a radius from an area shows whether they undo π and the square, or divide only." check: type: predict q: "A round rug has an area of 12.57 m². What is its radius?" options: ["2 m", "4 m", "6.28 m", "3.14 m"] actual: "2 m. 12.57 ÷ π = 4 = r², so r = √4 = 2 m." ``` What times itself, times π, makes 12.57? ## Run: find the radius ```step stage: run insight: "Searching for the radius that gives the area shows the two steps that undo A = πr²." try: { playground: board, starter: "circle.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "Find the radius of the 12.57 m² rug. Was your prediction right?", when: "r = 2", explain: "π × 2² = π × 4 ≈ 12.57 m²." } ``` Here's how the board's answer comes out. To find the radius from an area, undo each step: divide by $\pi$, then take the square root. $$r = \sqrt{A \div \pi}$$ For part of a circle, take the fraction: a semicircle is half the area $\frac{1}{2}\pi r^2$, a quarter circle a quarter. Its perimeter is the curved part plus the straight edges. Say which value of π you used (the π button, or 3.14). ## Investigate: backwards and in parts ```step stage: investigate insight: "Undo π then the square (Leo forgets the square root); a semicircle is half the area." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A circle has an area of 113.1 cm². Find its radius in cm." answer: 6 tolerance: 0.05 feedback: - ["36", "That is r². Take the square root."] explain: "113.1 ÷ π ≈ 36, and √36 = 6 cm." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#leo" text: "Leo finds the radius of a circle with area 50 cm². Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: circle-forget-root explain: "Line 2: 50 ÷ 3.14 is r², not r. Take the square root: r = √15.9 ≈ 4.0 cm." - check: type: question q: "How do you find the area of a semicircle of radius 4 cm?" options: ["Half of π × 4²", "π × 4² × 2", "Half of 2 × π × 4", "π × 2²"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That is two whole circles.", "That is half the circumference, a length.", "That is a circle of radius 2."] explain: "A semicircle is half the circle: ½ × π × 16 ≈ 25.1 cm²." ``` ### Backwards Here is the routine. ```worked 78.5 \div \pi \approx 25 :: Undo the π: this is r². r = \sqrt{25} = 5\ \text{cm} :: Undo the square with a square root. \pi \times 5^2 \approx 78.5 :: Check by going forwards. ``` ### Find the mistake Read Leo's working. Is 50 ÷ 3.14 the radius, or the radius squared? ### Semicircles ## Modify: tracks and rings ```step stage: modify insight: "Composite problems with circles: a semicircle, a running track's area and perimeter, and a target area on the board." try: { playground: board, starter: "circle.yml#free", height: 560 } tasks: - check: type: number q: "Find the area of a semicircle of radius 4 cm, in cm², to 1 decimal place." answer: 25.1 tolerance: 0.1 explain: "½ × π × 16 ≈ 25.1 cm²." - check: type: number q: "A running track's field is a 100 m by 60 m rectangle with a semicircle on each 60 m end. What is its area in m²? (Round to the nearest whole number.)" answer: 8827 tolerance: 2 explain: "The two semicircles make a circle of radius 30: π × 900 ≈ 2827 m². Plus the rectangle 6000 m²: about 8827 m²." - check: type: number q: "What is the perimeter of that field in metres, to the nearest whole number?" answer: 388 tolerance: 1 explain: "Two straights of 100 m, and the two semicircles make one circle of diameter 60: π × 60 ≈ 188.5 m. 200 + 188.5 ≈ 388 m." - starter: "circle.yml#free" check: { type: board, text: "Find the smallest radius (in steps of 0.5 m) whose area is more than 100 m².", when: "r = 6", explain: "r = 5.5 gives about 95 m²; r = 6 gives about 113 m²." } ``` ### A semicircle ### A track's area ### A track's perimeter ### Over 100 ## Practise: circle problems ```step stage: practise insight: "Radius from area, parts of circles, a ring and a semicircle's perimeter, mixed; forgetting the square root is the planted slip." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A circular pool cover has an area of 154 m². Find its radius in m." answer: 7 tolerance: 0.05 feedback: - ["49", "That is r². Take the square root."] explain: "154 ÷ π ≈ 49, and √49 = 7 m." - check: type: number q: "Find the area of a quarter circle of radius 10 cm, to 1 decimal place." answer: 78.5 tolerance: 0.1 explain: "¼ × π × 100 ≈ 78.5 cm²." - check: type: number q: "A ring is between circles of radius 5 cm and 3 cm. Find its area in cm², to 1 decimal place." answer: 50.3 tolerance: 0.2 explain: "π × 25 − π × 9 = π × 16 ≈ 50.3 cm²." - check: type: number q: "Find the perimeter of a semicircle of radius 5 cm (the curve and the diameter), to 1 decimal place." answer: 25.7 tolerance: 0.1 explain: "Half the circumference, π × 5 ≈ 15.7 cm, plus the diameter 10 cm: 25.7 cm." ``` ### Back to the radius ### A quarter circle ### A ring ### A semicircle's perimeter ## Make: a garden bed ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing a radius to meet an area range uses the formula backwards as a prediction, checked on the board." try: { playground: board, starter: "circle.yml#free", height: 560 } hint: ["25 ÷ π ≈ 8 and 30 ÷ π ≈ 9.5.", "Which radius has a square between those?"] check: { type: board, text: "A round garden bed must have an area between 25 and 30 m². Choose its radius.", when: "a > 25 and a < 30", explain: "r = 3 m: π × 9 ≈ 28.3 m²." } ``` Then work out how much edging the bed needs (its circumference), and say which value of π you used. ## Make: one large or two mediums, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Widths on a menu are diameters; the area of each pizza needs the radius squared, so the large is much bigger than it looks and two mediums can still beat it." hint: ["Halve each width to get the radius, then square it.", "Find the area of one large, then of two mediums, then take one from the other."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A large pizza is 30 cm across and a medium is 23 cm across. How many square centimetres more pizza do two mediums have than one large? Use the π button on your calculator and round to the nearest whole number." steps: - ["Large: $r = 15$, so $A = \\pi \\times 15^2 = \\pi \\times 225 \\approx 707$ cm²", "the radius is half of 30; square it before multiplying by π"] - ["Medium: $r = 11.5$, so $A = \\pi \\times 132.25 \\approx 415.5$ cm². Two mediums: about 831 cm²", "square 11.5, then double for two pizzas"] - ["$831 - 707 = 124$ cm²", "the two mediums have more"] picks: - step: 1 q: "How do you get a pizza's area from its width?" options: - "Halve it for the radius, square that, then multiply by π" - "Multiply the width by π" - "Square the width, then multiply by π" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That is the circumference, a length round the edge.", "That uses the width as the radius, which makes 4 times too much."] answer: "124" tolerance: 1 feedback: - ["496", "That uses each width as the radius. Halve the widths first."] - ["831", "That is the area of the two mediums. The question asks how much more than the large."] criteria: - "I halved each width to get a radius before squaring." - "I found the area of two mediums, not one." - "I subtracted in the right order and my answer is in cm²." explain: "Large: π × 15² ≈ 707 cm². Two mediums: 2 × π × 11.5² ≈ 831 cm². The difference is about 124 cm²." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The sizes are from a typical menu; prices are left out. Write each radius, square it, and keep the units, then type the difference. **Also used in** - **Food.** Menu sizes are widths, but the pizza you eat is area, so a bigger pizza is bigger than it looks. Value is area per dollar. - **Farming.** From the air, dry-country farms are green circles watered by an arm turning about a centre. The arm is the radius, and the corners of the paddock are what is left. - **Garden beds.** The edging is a circumference and the soil is an area. ```teacher summary: Students choose between circumference and area, find a radius from an area, and solve problems with semicircles, quarter circles, rings and tracks (AC9M8M03, node 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can choose the circumference or the area formula for a problem. - I can find the radius from an area. - I can solve problems with parts of circles. struggle: Working backwards from an area. Ask students to write the two steps of πr² forwards before they undo them. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need the area of a circle (previous lesson) and square roots. The one idea: ask whether the answer is a length (C = 2πr) or a space (A = πr²); to go back from an area, divide by π and take the square root. The common mistake is stopping at r² (Leo's mistake). Answers accept π from the calculator or 3.14; ask students to say which they used. Wider: composite shapes with circles (a stadium, a keyhole), and circles in First Nations Australian weaving designs, where the context is shared respectfully with local knowledge. running: - "Predict: ask for the two steps of πr² in order." - "Run: ask what area radius 1.5 gives, before moving the slider." - "Investigate: ask Leo to check his radius forwards." - "Modify: ask how the two semicircles of the track make one circle." - "Make: ask which formula the edging needs." - "Paper: one large against two mediums is worked in books; the page marks the difference and the reason for halving each width, then shows a model. Books out, and look for two radii squared, not the widths." stuck: - see: A student stops at r² when working backwards. ask: Is 15.9 the radius, or the radius squared? fix: Take the square root. - see: A student finds a semicircle's perimeter as half the circumference only. ask: "Walk round the semicircle: what straight part is there?" fix: Add the diameter. - see: A student uses the diameter in πr². ask: Radius or diameter? fix: Halve the diameter first. stretch: Is a 30 cm pizza more than twice as much as a 20 cm pizza? Compare their areas and prices from a real menu. support: "A two-column card: 'length round the edge' (C = 2πr) and 'space inside' (A = πr²)." leads: | This completes AC9M8M03. Where it leads: cylinders (Year 9), sectors and arc lengths (Year 10). exit: q: A circular pond has an area of 28.3 m². What is its radius? a: 28.3 ÷ π ≈ 9, and √9 = 3 m. explain: > Choose the formula: **circumference** $C = 2\pi r$ (a length) or **area** $A = \pi r^2$ (a space). From an area, $r = \sqrt{A \div \pi}$. Parts of circles: a semicircle is half the area; its perimeter is half the circumference plus the diameter. Say which value of π you used. ```
